answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each new identity to lock a scarce, time-bound stake before trading or voting. Its anchor graph grants access only after independent agents attest to the newcomer; equivocation or coordinated behavior slashes the deposit and revokes those attestations. The attacker must therefore fund every fake, wait for trust, and risk losing all deposits when the atlas links them, turning a cheap swarm into an ember-burning expense.
